root_cause.text: A lock ordering bug in Bluetooth L2CAP's l2cap_conn_del() caused it to call synchronous delayed-work cancellation while holding conn->lock, even though the cancelled work handlers also take conn->lock, leading to an AB-BA deadlock.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit explicitly states that l2cap_conn_del() called cancel_delayed_work_sync() for info_timer and id_addr_timer while holding conn->lock, and that l2cap_info_timeout() and l2cap_conn_update_id_addr() also acquire conn->lock; the patch fixes this by moving the cancellations before mutex_lock(&conn->lock) and replacing them with disable_delayed_work_sync().

agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE/commit explicitly states that l2cap_conn_del() called cancel_delayed_work_sync() for info_timer and id_addr_timer while holding conn->lock, and that l2cap_info_timeout() and l2cap_conn_update_id_addr() also acquire conn->lock; the patch fixes this by moving the cancellations before mutex_lock(&conn->lock) and replacing them with disable_delayed_work_sync().

intent_record.intent_summary: Cancel and flush L2CAP connection delayed timers during teardown to prevent asynchronous work from racing with freed connection state.
intent_record.what: Two new calls to disable_delayed_work_sync() were added at the start of l2cap_conn_del() to disable and synchronously flush conn->info_timer and conn->id_addr_timer before taking conn->lock and freeing connection resources.
intent_record.how: This prevents the connection's delayed work timers from running or remaining queued while the L2CAP connection is being deleted, avoiding races and potential use-after-free access to conn or its state during teardown.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove id_addr_timer cancellation from l2cap_conn_del() so delayed work cleanup is handled elsewhere during connection teardown.
intent_record.what: The call to cancel_delayed_work_sync(&conn->id_addr_timer) was removed from l2cap_conn_del() after ida_destroy(&conn->tx_ida) and before l2cap_unregister_all_users(conn).
intent_record.how: At runtime, l2cap_conn_del() no longer synchronously cancels the conn->id_addr_timer delayed work during connection teardown, allowing that timer to be handled elsewhere instead of being stopped at this point and avoiding teardown-time synchronization on that work item.

intent_record.intent_summary: Stop canceling the L2CAP info timer during connection deletion to avoid incorrect teardown behavior and leave timer cleanup to the proper path.
intent_record.what: The change removes a conditional block in l2cap_conn_del() that checked conn->info_state for L2CAP_INFO_FEAT_MASK_REQ_SENT and called cancel_delayed_work_sync(&conn->info_timer) when that flag was set.
intent_record.how: At runtime, connection deletion no longer cancels the info_timer delayed work from this code path, meaning teardown proceeds directly to hci_chan_del() and relies on timer handling elsewhere instead of conditionally synchronizing and stopping it here.

Remove id_addr_timer cancellation from l2cap_conn_del() so delayed work cleanup is handled elsewhere during connection teardown.
Stop canceling the L2CAP info timer during connection deletion to avoid incorrect teardown behavior and leave timer cleanup to the proper path.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly modifies L2CAP connection teardown by cancelling/flushing delayed work in l2cap_conn_del()-related paths, which is exactly where the deadlock root cause occurs: synchronous delayed-work cancellation interacting with conn->lock and work handlers that also take that lock.

The vulnerability is caused by cancelling delayed work from l2cap_conn_del() while holding conn->lock, which can deadlock if the work handler also takes that lock. Removing id_addr_timer cancellation from l2cap_conn_del() directly addresses that unsafe cancellation pattern during teardown.

The change removes cancellation of the L2CAP info timer from connection deletion, which directly affects the teardown path where synchronous work/timer cancellation under conn->lock caused the deadlock. Avoiding that cancellation in l2cap_conn_del() is aligned with fixing the lock-ordering bug.

candidates.rationale: This synchronous delayed-work cancellation was executed in l2cap_conn_del() while conn->lock was already held, and the cancelled work handler could also take conn->lock, creating the AB-BA deadlock described in the root cause.

This is another synchronous delayed-work cancellation inside l2cap_conn_del() under conn->lock; if the work function acquires conn->lock, cancel_delayed_work_sync() can deadlock waiting for work that is blocked on the same lock.

Holding conn->lock across later cancel_delayed_work_sync() calls is the locking side of the deadlock pattern; it establishes the problematic lock ordering that makes the synchronous cancellations unsafe.
